record.paper_title: Models, feedback control, and open problems of 3D bipedal robotic walking
record.original_question: Develop methods for maneuvering a 3D bipedal robot, such as turning or steering, that come with rigorous stability guarantees and also respect unilateral ground-contact constraints during the maneuver. The goal is not only to generate maneuvers heuristically, but to explain how a robot can change direction safely while maintaining dynamically stable walking.

evidence.quote: Relatively few papers have addressed the issue of maneuvering for bipedal robots, and even fewer have attempted to provide stability guarantees.
How to turn without violating unilateral ground contact constraints is not explained in this work.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a 3D bipedal robot modeled as a hybrid dynamical system: during each single-support phase the robot evolves according to Lagrangian dynamics with the stance foot acting as a pivot subject to unilateral ground-contact constraints (non-negative normal reaction force, friction-cone constraints, and no roll/slip of the stance foot), and at foot touchdown the state undergoes an impact reset map. A periodic walking gait is a hybrid limit cycle of this system that respects the unilateral contact constraints throughout, and is called dynamically stable if the associated Poincaré return map has a locally exponentially stable fixed point.

Develop a feedback control design methodology for executing maneuvers — in particular, turning or steering to change the robot's heading direction — that satisfies all of the following:

(i) Throughout the maneuver, the closed-loop trajectory satisfies the unilateral ground-contact constraints (positive normal force, friction-cone, and no foot rotation/slip) at every instant.

(ii) The maneuver is realized by transitioning between, or continuously deforming, families of parametrized periodic gaits (e.g., gaits parametrized by turning radius or heading rate), and the transitions admit a rigorous proof of stability — for instance, via a common Lyapunov function, a multiple Lyapunov function with dwell-time conditions, or contraction-based arguments applied to the hybrid Poincaré map.

(iii) The method yields verifiable certificates (analytical or computational) that the robot can change direction by a prescribed amount while maintaining dynamic stability and contact feasibility.

Provide either such a construction together with a proof, or establish obstructions showing why such guarantees cannot be obtained under stated assumptions on the model.
artifact.category_tag: Hybrid systems control of bipedal robots
artifact.status_search_result: Existing literature on 3D bipedal turning maneuvers (e.g., Gregg/Spong on planar/3D turning, follow-up work using HZD and QP-based controllers, and more recent dynamic-walking research) provides heuristic or simulation-validated turning controllers and partial stability analyses, but a complete framework giving rigorous stability guarantees for 3D turning maneuvers while provably respecting unilateral ground-contact constraints does not appear to have been established. The question is generally regarded as an open research direction in the dynamic-walking community.

status_evidence.title: Models, Feedback Control, and Open Problems of 3D Bipedal Robotic Walking
status_evidence.snippet: Relatively few papers have addressed maneuvering for bipedal robots, and even fewer have attempted to provide stability guarantees.
status_evidence.claim: Identifies maneuvering with stability guarantees and contact-constraint satisfaction as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Control of Dynamic Maneuvers for Bipedal Robots (PhD thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: Develops heuristics and controllers for dynamic maneuvers in bipeds with partial stability analysis.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress exists but rigorous guarantees for 3D turning under unilateral constraints remain incomplete.

status_evidence.title: Dynamic Walking: Toward Agile and Efficient Bipedal Robots
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses HZD/QP-based gait design and transitions for 3D bipeds.
status_evidence.claim: Recent advances continue to address but have not fully resolved the maneuvering-with-guarantees question.
